questions.topic: eGurukul · Congenital Heart Disease - Atrial Septal Defect
questions.stem: An atrial septal defect (ASD) is a hole in the heart between the upper chambers (atria). The hole increases the amount of blood that flows through the lungs. The condition is present at birth (congenital heart defect). Small atrial septal defects might be found by chance and never cause concern. Which of the following is NOT true about the atrial septal defect?

options.label: A
options.text: One of the most common etiologies of right heart dilation

options.label: B
options.text: Many ASDs are not discovered until adult life

options.label: C
options.text: Reverse splitting of the second heart sound

options.label: D
options.text: ECG commonly displays an incomplete right bundle branch block
